title: When the standard library is enough and the framework gets in the way

videos.script: This lesson takes a side. For a new Go API, start with the standard library. Add small libraries when you need them. Adopt a framework when you can name what it saves you. {{gap}} First, what changed. Go 1.22 closed the gap that made most routers necessary. Methods, wildcards, a 405. What it did not close is listed too. {{count}} Then the cost of doing it yourself. boxoffice already did, and you will count it: two hundred and sixty-nine lines of plumbing, and no new module. {{price}} Then the cost of the alternative. Fifty-five modules for Gin. And one import changed from Echo v5 to v4 breaks every handler in the file. {{ways}} A framework also gets in the way at particular moments. Its defaults, its handler type, its recycled context. {{earns}} And it earns its place in others. A large team that needs one way. Validation by tags. A measured bottleneck. {{decide}} The lesson ends with four questions, in the order that settles them.
